applicationInfo.name: retention-expiry-and-prune threat model
applicationInfo.description:
### Scope

This change ([proposal](proposal.md#what-changes)) removes the 90-day untagged ECR lifecycle rule, introduces one retention clock (Retain_Until = archive timestamp + configured days) whose authoritative copy is the pipeline-written S3 `worm-receipt.json` ([RETAIN-012]), defines two Prune_Candidate classes (expired bundle; unarchived manifest proven absent by positive not-found responses), and adds `cairn prune`, an operator verb that deletes named candidates under a dedicated, MFA-gated, per-project pruner role. The retention period is published by the stack to an SSM parameter that the archive stage reads and fails closed on. A stack-owned repository policy on each artifact repository ([ACCESS-010]) confines image deletes to the pruner role and lifecycle and repository-policy changes to the stack deployment role. A stack-owned prune audit log group, CloudTrail delete data events and [RETAIN-013] alarms record and surface every deletion, retention-configuration change, repository-policy change and trail change.

### Trust boundaries touched

The pruner is the first principal in the stack whose purpose is to delete evidence. Eligibility inputs cross from the untrusted producer zone (any ECR referrer and annotation) into the pruner's decision; [RETAIN-012] confines them to pre-filter and display. The Operator zone, untrusted for integrity under [ACCESS-006], is denied the retention-configuration knobs, repository-policy changes and alarm-wiring changes by [ACCESS-009]. The stack deployment role is now the single exception in the [ACCESS-010] repository policy for lifecycle and repository-policy changes, so it is the one trusted configuration principal on ECR. Principals in the account that the Operator policy does not bind are constrained on ECR only by that repository policy. WORM_Enabled=false in the current alpha, so S3 Object Lock is not active there; threats whose residual depends on Object Lock are flagged, because Object Lock cannot be added to a bucket after creation.

architecture.description:
### Components touched
1. `cdk/lib/constructs/repositories.ts`: the untagged lifecycle rule is removed, and the stack sets a repository policy on each artifact repository ([ACCESS-010]) that denies `ecr:BatchDeleteImage` to every principal except the project's pruner role and denies `ecr:PutLifecyclePolicy`, `ecr:DeleteLifecyclePolicy`, `ecr:SetRepositoryPolicy` and `ecr:DeleteRepositoryPolicy` to every principal except the stack deployment role, with no cross-account grant. `emptyOnDelete` stays `!isProd`.
2. `cdk/lib/constructs/iam-roles.ts`: a dedicated per-project pruner role ([ACCESS-007], [ACCESS-008]) whose trust policy requires `Bool aws:MultiFactorAuthPresent=true`, an `sts:SourceIdentity` equal to the caller's own identity, and a one-hour session. The Operator policy keeps its explicit DENY on `ecr:BatchDeleteImage`, `ecr:DeleteRepository`, `ecr:DeleteRepositoryPolicy`, `s3:DeleteObject*` and `dynamodb:DeleteItem`. [ACCESS-009] moves `ecr:PutLifecyclePolicy` and `ecr:SetRepositoryPolicy` from the Operator ALLOW to the explicit DENY, and adds DENY on `s3:PutLifecycleConfiguration`, `s3:PutBucketObjectLockConfiguration`, `s3:PutObjectLegalHold`, `ssm:PutParameter`, `ssm:LabelParameterVersion` and `ssm:DeleteParameter` on the retention parameter, `lambda:UpdateFunctionConfiguration` on archive-to-s3, and every change, disablement or retargeting of the [RETAIN-013] rules, alarms and topic (the Operator ALLOW holds `events:*Rule`, `events:PutTargets` and `cloudwatch:*AlarmActions` on `*` today).
3. `cdk/lib/constructs/lambda-functions.ts`: archive-to-s3 reads the retention-period SSM parameter; pipeline grants drop `dynamodb:DeleteItem`, `dynamodb:BatchWriteItem` ([ACCESS-007.02]) and `s3:PutObjectLegalHold` ([ACCESS-009.03]).
4. New stack resources: the repository policy ([ACCESS-010]), the retention-period SSM parameter ([RETAIN-007]), the never-expiring prune audit log group ([RETAIN-011]), and EventBridge alarm rules on CloudTrail events ([RETAIN-013]) covering image deletes, lifecycle and repository-policy changes, bucket lifecycle and Object Lock changes, SSM write/label/delete, archive-stage configuration and CloudTrail trail changes.
5. `cdk/scripts/deploy.sh`: the CloudTrail preflight also requires delete data events for the archive bucket and both tables ([ACCESS-004]).
6. `lambdas/archive_to_s3`: computes Retain_Until with day arithmetic, writes it to the S3 receipt copy, the ECR receipt referrer and the referrer annotation.
7. `cli/cairn_cli/prune.py`: report and named-digest delete in the order ECR referrers, ECR manifest, S3 versions, ControlClaims rows, index row, with an audit write before each step. The session comes from the operator's AWS profile (`role_arn`, `mfa_serial`, `source_identity`) through boto3's assume-role provider (design Decision 13); the CLI checks `sts:GetCallerIdentity` and refuses to delete unless the caller is a pruner-role session.
8. `cli/cairn_cli/tui/`: displays Retain_Until from the referrer annotation.
The architecture diagram is in [design.md](design.md#architecture).

dataflow.description:
### New and changed flows
1. A producer can push any manifest into the project repository, including a referrer whose artifactType is the WORM_Receipt type and whose annotations carry any retain-until value (crossing 1).
2. The stack deployment writes the retention period to SSM; archive-to-s3 reads it and fails closed on a missing or out-of-bounds value (crossings 4, 5).
3. archive-to-s3 writes S3 objects, the authoritative `worm-receipt.json` and Object Lock dates when WORM_Enabled=true, then the receipt referrer and annotation to ECR (crossings 6, 7).
4. The Operator is denied lifecycle, Object Lock, legal-hold, SSM and archive-stage configuration changes (crossing 8), repository-policy changes (crossing 9) and changes to the [RETAIN-013] alarm wiring (crossing 10).
5. The operator's AWS profile assumes the pruner role with MFA and a source identity (crossing 11). The pruner classifies from ECR, the S3 receipt copy and versions, and strongly consistent index reads (12, 13, 14), writes an audit record before each step (15), and deletes in fixed order (16, 17, 18).
6. CloudTrail records every call, including delete data events (19), and feeds the [RETAIN-013] alarm rules (20).
7. The TUI reads the annotation (21).
8. The stack deployment sets the repository policy and removes the lifecycle policy on each artifact repository (22).
9. Other principals in the account, which the Operator policy does not bind, meet the repository policy on ECR: `ecr:BatchDeleteImage` and policy changes are denied, but `ecr:DeleteRepository` and the ECR archive storage-class action are not named by [ACCESS-010] (23).
Crossing-to-threat map: 1 → T5, T6, T14, T16, T25; 2–3 → T4, T8; 4–5 → T7, T22; 6 → T9, T11; 7 → T5, T6; 8 → T1, T7; 9 → T19; 10 → T20; 11 → T2, T17, T21; 12 → T5, T12, T24, T25; 13 → T5, T10, T11, T24; 14 → T4, T24, T26; 15 → T3, T23; 16 → T2, T12; 17 → T2, T10; 18 → T13, T26; 19 → T3; 20 → T2, T3, T20, T27; 21 → T16; 22 → T19, T28; 23 → T27, T28.

assumptions.content: A deployment with WORM_Enabled=false is non-production per [WORM-008]. S3 Object Lock legal holds cannot exist in such a bucket, so the legal-hold veto of [RETAIN-004] has effect only under WORM_Enabled=true.

Each deployment serves one project repository. validate-bundle already rejects a bundle whose claimed org/tenant/project differs from the IAM-enforced ECR repository path (libs/validation crosscheck.py), so the canonical S3 key prefix ({org}/{tenant}/{project}/{digest}/) and the Metadata_Index key (pk={tenant}, sk={project}#{digest}) are derivable from deployment coordinates plus the named digest alone.

deploy.sh refuses to deploy without an active CloudTrail trail with management-event logging and, under [ACCESS-004] as amended, data events for archive-bucket object deletes and Metadata_Index and ControlClaims item deletes. The trail itself is account-level and outside the stack, so the preflight proves coverage at deploy time only.
S3 Object Lock Compliance mode denies DeleteObjectVersion before ObjectLockRetainUntilDate for every principal, including the account root, and allows retention to be extended but never shortened.

An Artifact_Producer is untrusted for content. It holds repo-scoped ecr:PutImage (so it can push any manifest, including a referrer with any artifactType, subject and annotations) and holds no S3 or DynamoDB write permission.

The Operator ([ACCESS-006]) is untrusted for integrity. The pruner role is assumed in a separate, MFA-authenticated session by a designated human who is accountable for deletion; the Operator policy's explicit DENY on deletes means one session carrying both policies cannot prune, but one human may hold both entitlements in separate sessions.

Whether ECR removes an untagged referrer when its subject is deleted is unverified (design Context item 3). This model does not depend on it; it treats any such referrer as an orphan that the unarchived-manifest class covers.

CloudTrail records the assumed-role ARN and, when set, the sts:SourceIdentity of every API call made in a pruner session, independently of anything cairn prune writes. CloudWatch Logs PutLogEvents content is not recorded by CloudTrail.

Verified in cdk/lib/constructs/iam-roles.ts: the Operator ALLOW statements grant no ssm write, no logs write, no cloudtrail write, no sts:AssumeRole, no cloudformation write, no lambda:GetLayerVersion, no iam:PassRole, and no DynamoDB, Lambda or CloudWatch Logs resource-policy action, so those paths are implicitly denied. The Operator guardrail already DENIES ecr:DeleteRepository and ecr:DeleteRepositoryPolicy. The ALLOW statements grant ecr:PutLifecyclePolicy and ecr:SetRepositoryPolicy on the artifact namespace and events:PutRule, events:PutTargets, events:DisableRule, cloudwatch:PutMetricAlarm and cloudwatch:DisableAlarmActions on *; [ACCESS-009] as amended overrides each of these with an explicit DENY.

The stack deployment (CloudFormation execution role) is trusted to set the retention period, lifecycle configuration, the [ACCESS-010] repository policy and alarm wiring, and is the only exception in that repository policy for lifecycle and repository-policy changes. [RETAIN-013] makes its retention-relevant changes visible; it is not otherwise constrained by this change.

The Operator cannot act as the stack deployment role: it holds no sts:AssumeRole on the CDK bootstrap roles and no cloudformation write (A9). Who may assume the CDK deploy role is set by the account's bootstrap trust, outside this stack. A principal that can drive CloudFormation with the execution role is equivalent to the stack deployment (A10).

mitigations.content: The Operator policy keeps its explicit DENY on ecr:BatchDeleteImage, s3:DeleteObject, s3:DeleteObjectVersion, s3:PutObjectRetention, s3:BypassGovernanceRetention and dynamodb:DeleteItem (resource *), so a principal carrying the Operator policy cannot prune even if the pruner policy is also attached.

metadata.value: Exists today in cdk/lib/constructs/iam-roles.ts OperatorIntegrityAndBlastRadiusGuardrail; kept unchanged by this change.

mitigations.content: Per [ACCESS-009]: remove ecr:PutLifecyclePolicy and ecr:SetRepositoryPolicy from the Operator ALLOW statement OperatorEcrSubstrateManagement and add ecr:PutLifecyclePolicy, ecr:SetRepositoryPolicy, ecr:DeleteRepositoryPolicy, s3:PutLifecycleConfiguration, s3:PutBucketObjectLockConfiguration, s3:PutObjectLegalHold, ssm:PutParameter, ssm:LabelParameterVersion and ssm:DeleteParameter on the retention parameter, and lambda:UpdateFunctionConfiguration on archive-to-s3 to the Operator explicit DENY, with CDK jest assertions for [ACCESS-009.01], [ACCESS-009.02] and [ACCESS-009.04].

metadata.value: Specified by [ACCESS-009]. M27 adds the resource-side lock for principals outside the Operator policy.

mitigations.content: Per [RETAIN-013]: EventBridge rules on CloudTrail events ecr:PutLifecyclePolicy, ecr:DeleteLifecyclePolicy, ecr:SetRepositoryPolicy, ecr:DeleteRepositoryPolicy, s3:PutBucketLifecycle (PutLifecycleConfiguration), s3:PutBucketObjectLockConfiguration, ssm:PutParameter, ssm:LabelParameterVersion and ssm:DeleteParameter on the retention parameter, and lambda:UpdateFunctionConfiguration on archive-to-s3, targeting the SNS alarm topic with caller principal and resource; jest assertions over the synthesized event patterns.

metadata.value: Specified by [RETAIN-013] items 2 to 4. Catches changes made by the stack deployment, which [ACCESS-009] does not bind. M28 keeps it out of the Operator's reach.

mitigations.content: CDK synth assertion and jest test for [RETAIN-006.01]: no artifact ECR repository carries a lifecycle policy and the archive bucket lifecycle has only storage-class transitions, no Expiration or NoncurrentVersionExpiration.

Per [ACCESS-007]: the pruner is a dedicated per-project IAM role whose trust policy names only designated principals, requires MFA and sts:SourceIdentity, and sets MaxSessionDuration to one hour; it is not assumable by the Operator, producer, signing, alias-mover, auditor or any Lambda execution role. Its deletes are ecr:BatchDeleteImage on the project repository ARN, s3:DeleteObjectVersion under {org}/{tenant}/{project}/*, and dynamodb:DeleteItem on Metadata_Index and ControlClaims under dynamodb:LeadingKeys={tenant}. It holds no kms:Decrypt.

metadata.value: Specified by [ACCESS-007] and design Decision 8. LeadingKeys binds only the partition key (tenant), see T26. Trust-policy implementation detail is in M29.

mitigations.content: Per [RETAIN-013.01]: an EventBridge rule on CloudTrail ecr:BatchDeleteImage against the artifact namespace (a management event, always logged), targeting the SNS alarm topic with the caller principal and image digests, for every principal and every path, including raw API calls in a pruner session.

metadata.value: Specified by [RETAIN-013.01]. M28 keeps it out of the Operator's reach. Does not see DeleteRepository (T27, M36).

mitigations.content: The pruner grant excludes s3:BypassGovernanceRetention, s3:PutObjectRetention, s3:PutObjectLegalHold and every ECR or S3 lifecycle mutation ([ACCESS-008]), with a jest assertion over the synthesized policy document. The pruner may append to the prune audit log group but holds no logs:DeleteLogGroup, logs:DeleteLogStream or logs:PutRetentionPolicy ([ACCESS-008.03]).
Under WORM_Enabled=true, S3 Object Lock Compliance mode on every archive object version denies an early DeleteObjectVersion for every principal ([WORM-001], [ACCESS-008.02]).

metadata.value: Exists today: archive.ts objectLockEnabled=wormEnabled. Active only when WORM_Enabled=true, which the alpha does not set; production must set it at bucket creation.

mitigations.content: Per [RETAIN-011]: cairn prune writes a structured audit record to the stack-owned, never-expiring prune audit log group before each delete step and after each item's outcome, naming the STS caller identity, digest, class, reason, step and outcome; an audit write failure stops the next delete step.

metadata.value: Specified by [RETAIN-011] and design Decision 14. The record body is client-asserted (A8); the non-repudiation anchor is CloudTrail (M10, M30).

mitigations.content: Per [ACCESS-004]: the deploy CloudTrail preflight fails unless a trail logs data events for object-version deletes on the archive bucket and item deletes on the Metadata_Index and ControlClaims tables. As a task-level addition, raise the access-log bucket expiration (90 days today) to at least the audit horizon.

metadata.value: Specified by [ACCESS-004.02] and [ACCESS-004.03]. The access-log expiration is not in the spec and lands as a task.

mitigations.content: Per [RETAIN-012] and [RETAIN-004.04]: cairn prune derives the S3 prefix and the Metadata_Index key from the deployment's org/tenant/project coordinates and the named digest, never from a receipt body or annotation; refuses when more than one WORM_Receipt referrer exists or the ECR receipt disagrees with the S3 copy; and classifies an expired bundle only when at least one S3 object version exists under the derived prefix.

metadata.value: Specified. Closes the forged-receipt redirect and the vacuous all-versions-expired case.

mitigations.content: Per [RETAIN-012] and [RETAIN-009]: the authoritative Retain_Until is read from the pipeline-written S3 copy {prefix}worm-receipt.json (producers have no S3 write) and, under WORM_Enabled=true, from the latest ObjectLockRetainUntilDate of the prefix's versions; the ECR annotation is a pre-filter and display value only.

Per [RETAIN-008] as amended: a content manifest is an unarchived-manifest candidate only with no referrer of any kind, no Metadata_Index record and no S3 object under its derived prefix, each absence proven by a positive not-found response; a validation-rejected bundle, which carries a Producer_Attestation_Referrer, is never junk.

Replace metadataTable.grantReadWriteData (validate-bundle, update-metadata) and controlsTable.grantReadWriteData (update-metadata) with explicit GetItem/PutItem/UpdateItem/Query grants that exclude dynamodb:DeleteItem and dynamodb:BatchWriteItem. sign-bundle holds metadataTable.grantWriteData, which also includes both actions; [ACCESS-007.02] covers every pipeline role, so narrow that grant too.

metadata.value: Specified by [ACCESS-007.02], which now covers DeleteItem and BatchWriteItem for every pipeline role.

mitigations.content: Replace archiveBucket.grantPut(archiveToS3) with explicit s3:PutObject and s3:PutObjectRetention so the archive Lambda no longer holds s3:PutObjectLegalHold (CDK grantPut includes it), and assert that no role other than a future legal-hold role (#4) holds s3:PutObjectLegalHold.

Immediately before the first ECR delete of an item, cairn prune re-reads retention and legal-hold status for every S3 object version of the bundle ([RETAIN-005] item 3, [RETAIN-010]); the S3 step itself is the final authority under WORM_Enabled=true.

metadata.value: Specified by [RETAIN-005.03] and [RETAIN-010.03]; the residual window is seconds.

mitigations.content: Per [RETAIN-010]: when a named digest's ECR parts are already gone, re-classification uses the S3 receipt copy and the S3 object versions under the derived prefix, and the Metadata_Index record is kept until every S3 object version is deleted.

Per [RETAIN-010]: cairn prune deletes the bundle's ControlClaims rows before the Metadata_Index row, with the pruner DeleteItem grant covering the ControlClaims table under the same LeadingKeys scope.

Per [RETAIN-008.05]: an orphan referrer or referrers-tag-schema index is classified only when the subject lookup returns ImageNotFoundException for that exact digest; throttling, AccessDenied or any other error refuses the item and the report names the failed check. The subject check runs again at delete time ([RETAIN-005] item 3).

Add a CloudWatch alarm on the repository image count against the ECR images-per-repository service quota, and a runbook entry for requesting a quota increase, since no lifecycle rule now bounds the count.

metadata.value: Risk accepted by the user: alarm deferred to #34 AC 5; runbook quota check is the interim control.

mitigations.content: The deploy runbook states that rollback past this change re-adds the 90-day untagged rule and is allowed only before any bundle is 90 days old, and that the Notation --force-referrers-tag=false fix ships after this change (design Migration Plan steps 3 and 4).

metadata.value: Procedural; design Migration Plan steps 3 and 4.

mitigations.content: The TUI routes every rendered cell through its terminal-render safety helper (_safe in cli/cairn_cli/tui/app.py).

The TUI parses the retain-until annotation strictly as RFC 3339 UTC and shows unknown otherwise ([TUI-016.02]), labels the value as producer-visible receipt metadata, and offers no delete action ([TUI-016.03]).

Per [RETAIN-007] and [ACCESS-009]: the stack publishes the retention period to an SSM parameter that only the stack deployment writes; archive-to-s3 reads it and fails the archive with artifact.archive-failed, writing no object and no receipt, when it is missing, not a whole number, or outside 1 to 36,135; the Operator is denied ssm:PutParameter on it and lambda:UpdateFunctionConfiguration on archive-to-s3.
If any prune read needs decryption, grant kms:Decrypt to the pruner only with kms:ViaService limited to ECR and S3 in the deployment region, as design Decision 8 anticipates.

metadata.value: Design Decision 8 states the pruner needs no kms:Decrypt; keep it that way.

mitigations.content: Accept that a non-production stack teardown (isProd=false) empties the archive bucket via the CDK auto-delete-objects custom resource and the ECR repository via emptyOnDelete. These run only on stack deletion through CloudFormation and are absent when isProd=true. [RETAIN-005] carves non-production teardown out of the only-sanctioned-path wording.

Per [ACCESS-009] item 1, [ACCESS-009.04] and [ACCESS-010]: deny the Operator ecr:SetRepositoryPolicy and ecr:DeleteRepositoryPolicy, and have the stack own a repository policy on each artifact repository that DENIES ecr:BatchDeleteImage to every principal whose aws:PrincipalArn is not the project's pruner role, DENIES ecr:PutLifecyclePolicy, ecr:DeleteLifecyclePolicy, ecr:SetRepositoryPolicy and ecr:DeleteRepositoryPolicy to every principal whose aws:PrincipalArn is not the stack deployment role, and holds no Allow for a principal outside the account. Add jest assertions for [ACCESS-010.01] to [ACCESS-010.03] over the synthesized RepositoryPolicyText, and [RETAIN-013.02] alarms on repository-policy changes (M3).

metadata.value: Specified by [ACCESS-009] and [ACCESS-010] (closes T19). A resource-policy DENY binds every principal, including ones whose identity policy the Operator does not control.

mitigations.content: Per [ACCESS-009] item 5 and [ACCESS-009.05]: add to the Operator explicit DENY events:PutRule, events:PutTargets, events:RemoveTargets, events:DisableRule and events:DeleteRule on the [RETAIN-013] rule ARNs; cloudwatch:DisableAlarmActions, cloudwatch:PutMetricAlarm and cloudwatch:DeleteAlarms on any alarm that backs them; and sns:Unsubscribe, sns:SetTopicAttributes, sns:DeleteTopic and sns:RemovePermission on the alarm topic. Add jest assertions for [ACCESS-009.05]. Order this before the first pruner deployment.

metadata.value: Specified by [ACCESS-009] (closes T20). Keeps the detective layer that the T2, T7 and T19 residuals rely on out of the Operator's reach.

mitigations.content: Per [ACCESS-007] and design Decision 13: implement the trust policy with Bool aws:MultiFactorAuthPresent=true (never BoolIfExists), name the designated principals by exact ARN, and constrain sts:SourceIdentity to the caller's own name (StringEquals sts:SourceIdentity=${aws:username} for IAM users). The runbook gives the exact profile (role_arn, mfa_serial, source_identity, duration_seconds=3600). If designated principals are federated or IAM Identity Center sessions, which carry no aws:MultiFactorAuthPresent in a chained role session, record the substitution of IdP-enforced MFA and an IdP-asserted source identity as a design decision with its own trust-policy test, rather than relaxing the condition. Add jest assertions over the synthesized trust policy, and CLI tests that a non-pruner caller is refused before any delete with a clear message.

metadata.value: Specified by [ACCESS-007] and design Decision 13 (T21). The federated-principal branch is task-level.

mitigations.content: Per [RETAIN-013] item 5 and [RETAIN-013.03]: alarm on cloudtrail:StopLogging, cloudtrail:DeleteTrail, cloudtrail:UpdateTrail and cloudtrail:PutEventSelectors for trails in the deployment's account, so the data-event coverage proven at deploy time cannot be removed silently. The audit record carries the assumed-role ARN and SourceIdentity that CloudTrail records independently. The deploy runbook states that an organization trail is changed from the management account, where these alarms do not fire, and names who watches that account.

metadata.value: Specified by [RETAIN-013] (T3). The organization-trail note is task-level.

mitigations.content: Per [ACCESS-009] item 3 and [RETAIN-013] item 4: deny the Operator ssm:PutParameter, ssm:LabelParameterVersion and ssm:DeleteParameter on the retention-period parameter, and alarm on all three. archive-to-s3 reads the parameter by name with no label or version selector, and the deploy runbook requires an explicit acknowledgement when a production deployment lowers retentionPeriodDays.

metadata.value: Specified by [ACCESS-009] and [RETAIN-013] (T22). The read-by-name rule and runbook acknowledgement are task-level.

mitigations.content: cairn prune resolves the bucket, table and repository names from the stack's published outputs, never from free-form input; before it classifies any item as an unarchived manifest it proves its coordinates with a positive-found check in the same run (the project prefix lists at least one object, DescribeTable shows the expected key schema); it counts delete markers as present versions; and the S3 delete step removes delete markers as well as versions so the index row is not stranded.

When [RETAIN-012.02] refuses an item for multiple receipts, the report names every receipt referrer digest and which one matches the S3 receipt copy. File a follow-up issue for a sanctioned path to remove a non-matching decoy referrer whose subject is present.

metadata.value: Task plus follow-up issue (T25). The refusal is fail-safe; this only restores the ability to prune.

mitigations.content: Accept that the pruner's dynamodb:DeleteItem is scoped to the tenant partition key, because IAM cannot condition on a sort-key prefix. cairn prune derives the sort key from its own project, and each deployment serves one project today (A2).

metadata.value: Risk accepted (T26). Revisit when a deployment serves more than one project per tenant.

mitigations.content: Before an item's first delete step, cairn prune checks that the session has enough remaining lifetime to finish the item and stops cleanly before starting if not; on any audit or session failure mid-item it exits non-zero with the step named, leaving the item resumable through [RETAIN-010].

Add ecr:DeleteRepository and the ECR archive storage-class action (ecr:UpdateImageStorageClass) to the [ACCESS-010] repository-policy DENY for every principal except the stack deployment role, and add DeleteRepository and the storage-class change to the [RETAIN-013] alarm set. Prefer a spec amendment to [ACCESS-010] and [RETAIN-013] so the guarantee in [ACCESS-010.01] holds as stated; otherwise land it as a task with a jest assertion over the synthesized repository policy and event patterns.

metadata.value: Recommended (T27). Verify the exact IAM action name for the ECR archive storage class at implementation time.

mitigations.content: Write each [ACCESS-010] DENY as Principal * with a Condition ArnNotEquals on aws:PrincipalArn, never as NotPrincipal. Take the deployment-role ARN from the stack synthesizer's CloudFormation execution role, and assert in jest that the exception equals it. Run the migration deploy in alpha first and confirm in CloudTrail that DeleteLifecyclePolicy and SetRepositoryPolicy are called by that role. Add a non-production teardown check that emptyOnDelete still empties the repository under the new policy, or except the deployment role from the image-delete DENY when isProd=false only.

metadata.value: Task-level (T28, T18). Order before the first deploy of this change.

threats.prerequisites: holding the Operator policy
threats.threatAction: attach an age-based untagged lifecycle rule to the project repository after this change removes it
threats.threatImpact: ECR silently reaping every untagged referrer and archived manifest, so cairn verify fails for every affected bundle with no delete call ever made
threats.statement: An operator holding the Operator policy can attach an age-based untagged lifecycle rule to the project repository after this change removes it, which leads to ECR silently reaping every untagged referrer and archived manifest, so cairn verify fails for every affected bundle with no delete call ever made, resulting in reduced integrity and availability of Notation signature referrers, WORM_Receipt referrers, Artifact_Bundle ECR manifests

metadata.value: Was High. [ACCESS-009] denies the Operator ecr:PutLifecyclePolicy and s3:PutLifecycleConfiguration, [ACCESS-010] denies ecr:PutLifecyclePolicy to every principal except the stack deployment role through the repository policy, [RETAIN-006.01] asserts no lifecycle rule at synth, and [RETAIN-013.02] alarms on any lifecycle change. With T19 closed, no principal outside the deployment can add a rule.

threats.prerequisites: holding an MFA-authenticated pruner role session for one project
threats.threatAction: call ecr:BatchDeleteImage, s3:DeleteObjectVersion or dynamodb:DeleteItem directly with the AWS CLI instead of through cairn prune
threats.threatImpact: deleting the ECR verification surface of a retained bundle in either WORM mode, and any bundle in full under WORM_Enabled=false, because eligibility checks run only in the client
threats.statement: A designated pruner holding an MFA-authenticated pruner role session for one project can call ecr:BatchDeleteImage, s3:DeleteObjectVersion or dynamodb:DeleteItem directly with the AWS CLI instead of through cairn prune, which leads to deleting the ECR verification surface of a retained bundle in either WORM mode, and any bundle in full under WORM_Enabled=false, because eligibility checks run only in the client, resulting in reduced integrity and availability of Artifact_Bundle ECR manifests and referrers, S3 archive object versions, Metadata_Index rows

metadata.value: Was High. [ACCESS-007] makes the pruner a dedicated per-project role with designated principals, Bool aws:MultiFactorAuthPresent, a caller-bound sts:SourceIdentity and a one-hour session; [ACCESS-010] makes it the only principal that can delete images; [RETAIN-013.01] alarms on every image delete and [ACCESS-009.05] keeps the Operator from silencing it; CloudTrail logs ECR deletes as management events and S3/DynamoDB deletes as data events ([ACCESS-004]). The residual is the inherent insider risk of any delete grant: a designated, MFA-authenticated human can use the raw API to delete the ECR copy of a retained bundle in either WORM mode (ECR has no Object Lock), and the whole bundle under WORM_Enabled=false. Under WORM_Enabled=true the S3 copy survives and can be re-pushed ([WORM-007]). Detected, not prevented.

threats.prerequisites: who deletes S3 object versions or index rows
threats.threatAction: deny or conceal the deletion by skipping or forging the client-written audit record and relying on the account-level trail having lost its delete data-event coverage after deployment
